view: Consensus (six members, simple mean): 2w about 34 up / 34 range / 33 down, this_quarter 36/36/28, next_quarter 46/28/26, i.e. 'idiosyncratic governance shock, wide tails into the print, fades over two quarters; tactical Wait, strategic Accumulate/Hold'. The strongest opposite case is that the weakness is not mainly a fading key-person shock but a year-long competitive and estimate de-rating (NVDA/SOX -43.9% over 52w, AMD +169.15% YTD, consensus EPS already implying lower margins), so the up-skew on the quarters leans on a bull-era base rate and tiny conditional samples; I put this_quarter and next_quarter close to balanced between up and down.

probabilities.defs: 2w ±5%, quarters ±10%, vs price_at_call 165.785. next_2_weeks: up = close > 174.07, down = close < 157.50, range between, measured at the 2026-11-26 close (see notes: likely a market holiday). this_quarter: to the last close of 2026-12-31; next_quarter: to the last close of 2027-03-31; up > 182.36, down < 149.21, range between. up + range + down = 100.

evidence.point: Outside view 33/45/22 (n=258). I land at 33/32/35, essentially with the consensus: range -13 for earnings plus a 5.9% daily ATR, down +13. I do not dissent on 2w; the earnings binary is genuinely two-sided and nobody can see positioning.

Outside view 39/43/18 (n=253). I move to 31/36/33 (up -8, range -7, down +15), further down than every member. The -10% line 149.21 is only about 1.7 daily ATRs (9.86) below price, and the window holds the print, opex 2026-11-20, FOMC 2026-12-09 and CPI 2026-12-10 (fcst 3.9 vs 3.7) with an unresolved DOJ track.

Outside view 50/31/19 (n=247), but the sample is 260 weekly bars from 2021-11-22, almost all of it inside NVDA's AI bull regime (price still +34.1% above the 200W SMA): its 50% up rate is regime drift, not a neutral prior for a stock whose relative trend has broken. The window to 2027-03-31 is also about 20 weeks, longer than 13w, so range should be smaller. I move to 41/25/34.

NVDA/SOX ratio fell 43.9% over 52w (27.9202 -> 15.6556) and 13.7% over 13w, and NVDA vs SPX -23.2% over 52w. This underperformance started long before the governance headlines, so 'key-person shocks fade within one to two quarters' (narrative) does not explain it and should not be expected to reverse it.

Same week: AMD +30.2%, AVGO +17.46%, SOX +7.99% while NVDA -15.45%; AMD +169.15% YTD vs NVDA -12.67%. A 45-point weekly spread to its closest competitor is at least as consistent with a competitive share shift (cause not in slice) as with a governance discount. Macro and relative_strength attribute the gap to governance by inference; nobody has read the AMD/AVGO side. If it is share loss, it does not fade with the news cycle.

Derived from slice numbers (approximate): shares about 24.08B (market cap 3,992.5B / 165.785). Next-quarter consensus EPS 2.47 on revenue 108.67B implies a net margin near 55% vs 63.7% TTM, and an EPS below the roughly 2.55 implied for last quarter (96.22B x 63.7%) despite +12.9% revenue. Next-FY EPS 9.29 is below 4 x 2.47 = 9.88. The estimates already embed margin compression and a growth stall, so the 17.85x forward P/E is 'cheap' only if the estimates hold; fiscal-label convention (tv_fundamentals.history_labels) may also be off.

FCF fell to 21.40B from 48.59B in one quarter while total debt rose from 12.81B to 38.86B. Causes are not in slice. Together with the margin compression implied by estimates, this is a quality-of-earnings question the bullish quarter tilt (fundamentals 52 up next_quarter) does not price.

Price is 5.3% below the 100W SMA (175.09) and 18.9% below the 200D SMA, with the 179.92-185.22 gap overhead; weekly MACD -1.8 below signal 4.54, weekly summary SELL. Counted once as the momentum group. An up outcome this quarter (>182.36) needs the whole resistance stack cleared; down (<149.21) needs one more ATR-sized leg.

Real 10y 2.66, 10y 5.0, CPI 3.7 heading to a 3.9 forecast, RSP +4.03% vs SPY -2.12% over 1m: the market is rotating out of mega-cap leaders. Not the driver of the week, but a headwind that removes the 'macro tailwind' leg from any rebound story; beta vs SPX 1.42-1.75 means an index pullback hits NVDA harder.

One evidence group: DOJ inquiry into Megaspeed (~240,000 chips / $7.5bn alleged), board probe (Wachtell Lipton), a senator calling for resignation and a revived export-restriction push. No finding and no charge: TB1-TB3 have not fired. DOJ timelines are open-ended, so the overhang can outlast both quarters; it is a reason for fat tails, not for a fade-and-recover base case.

Hunt - small samples: n=4 (13w 100% up) and n=13 (RSI<=36, 13w 69% up) are overlapping weekly windows, so the effective number of independent episodes is probably one to three. Worse, nobody verified the condition applies: week_change_pct is -11.2% from 186.64 and the 2w change is not in slice. Several members used these to 'stop going further bearish'; they should carry near-zero weight.

Hunt - signal on an open bar: weekly RSI 33.3/33.13 is not oversold (threshold 30) and the bar is open; the April 2025 low printed 35.7, so 'lowest since 2023' is not a bottom marker. Lessons-log 2026-11-11 already caught this once.

Hunt - analyst targets as evidence: fundamentals and narrative both use the lowest target 180 as a key level, narrative cites 58 of 73 buys as 'thesis intact', and the forward P/E uses the same analysts' EPS 9.29. News says analysts are cutting targets. Ratings, targets and EPS estimates are one lagging group and should not support a level or a probability.

Hunt - unread page: options positioning failed. The consensus 2w tail split (down-skewed), sentiment's 'distribution not capitulation' read and every 'earnings widens tails' adjustment depend on the implied move and hedging that nobody can see. CNN F&G is partial and AAII (2026-11-04) predates this week's leg. Hyperscaler capex and guidance are not in any slice, so TB4 status is unmonitored, not 'not fired'.

Hunt - anchoring: technical's key levels (164.27, 161.98, 154.53, 140.76, 123.61) are the proposed ladder's anchors, and the linear fibs are scale-dependent (log 0.65 = 81.83, 0.618 = 74.07). Fundamentals frames -31.9% from the 243.37 ATH as 'multiple compression'. The ATH and the ladder are setting the levels, not independent support evidence.

Hunt - double counting: all six members cut 2w range by 5-15 points for the same two facts (earnings inside the window, 5.9% ATR) and four of six attribute the week to the same governance story. The chair should treat this as one adjustment and one hypothesis, not six confirmations.

Hunt - earnings treated as predictable: fundamentals leans up on both quarters pre-print because valuation is 'cheap vs growth', which implicitly assumes the print confirms estimates; narrative calls the call 'the first chance to address governance', assuming a positive framing. Before the print the honest stance is near-symmetric; after it, update on guidance, gross margin vs 74.7% and the FCF/debt explanation, not on the headline beat.

key_levels.why: this_quarter / next_quarter down line (-10%); about 1.7 daily ATRs below price, and roughly 16x the 9.29 next-FY EPS estimate (support only if the estimate survives the print).
Linear fib 0.618 / L2 zone; two daily closes below it after the print would favour my quarter down bucket.
Apr 2026 swing low, already within about 1% of price; failure confirms the 2026 range low has broken.
100W SMA; a weekly close back above it is the first evidence that the consensus 'shock fades' view is right.
NVDA/SOX ratio now; further decline while SOX rises supports the share-shift case, a move back toward 18.1331 supports the consensus.

what_would_change_my_mind: Check 1 (2026-11-17 print, judged on the 2026-11-18 close): guidance above the 108.67B revenue / 2.47 EPS bar with gross margin holding near 74.7% and a temporary explanation for FCF 21.40B vs 48.59B and debt 38.86B, plus a close above 174.07, would move me back to the consensus on both quarters (about +8 up, -8 down). A guide that confirms margin compression or a close below 157.50 would move this_quarter down to about 40.

Check 2 (weeks ending 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-27): NVDA outperforming SOX and the NVDA/SOX ratio rising off 15.6556 toward 18.1331 would show the gap was governance and is closing; the ratio still falling while SOX rises confirms a competitive share shift and keeps my quarter down tilt.
Check 3 (weekly closes 2026-11-13 through 2026-12-31): a weekly close above 175.09 (100W SMA), or above 186 (gap filled), falsifies my this_quarter call; two daily closes below 154.53 confirm it.
Any TB1-TB4 event, or an Nvidia 10-Q legal-proceedings disclosure of a DOJ/BIS matter, would push me further down; a board/DOJ statement clearing Nvidia and Huang would push me toward the consensus.
notes_for_chair: Pre-mortem for my own view: if the red team is badly wrong in three months, the likely reason is that the 3.6x volume week was the capitulation low and the print reset the narrative, so the n=4 / n=13 samples happened to be right; I would then have over-weighted a 52w relative trend that reverses quickly.

Scoring definition: 2026-11-26 is the fourth Thursday of November (US Thanksgiving), when US markets are normally closed. Please fix the 2w scoring close (2026-11-25 or 2026-11-27) before logging, or the question is not scorable.
The price_at_call 165.785 is an intraday open-bar price below the recorded week low 165.89, while base rates are built on weekly closes. Small, but the 2w buckets are measured from a non-close.
Data conflicts to reconcile before anyone cites them: nvda_perf_w -15.45% vs week_change_pct -11.2%; beta vs SPX 1.42 (59w) vs 1.75 (1y).

Do not average the six members as six independent votes: they share the same earnings/ATR adjustment and four share the same governance attribution. Weight the dissenting cause (competitive share shift) explicitly, because no slice can currently test it beyond the relative-performance numbers.

Before the print: I agree with tactical Wait (blackout window 2026-11-12 to 2026-11-17 is in force). After the print: the competitive vs governance question, not the beat, decides whether strategic Accumulate in stages is warranted. Reduce is not available (no recorded position, no thesis break fired).

Ladder: L1 (162-164) and L2 (154-157) are under one ATR apart and lean on linear fibs; if the share-shift case is right, both could fill on a single post-print move, putting 33.3% of the budget to work at an average of 158.42 before the cause is known. Owner's decision; the committee audits only.
Thesis breaks: TB1-TB3 not fired on the slice evidence; TB4 cannot be assessed because hyperscaler capex is not in any slice.
